payload.authority: researcher decision under the preregistration's own amendment clause, taken after stage 0 was executed as a simulation-only probe and before any calibration partition value was read. Stage 0 was NOT frozen: its outcome was STAGE0_ADJUDICATION_REQUIRED, which is the state this amendment adjudicates.

calibration_preregistration.bounds.physi.after: A preregistered, simulation-only feasibility rule. A value is FEASIBLE when all four classes, at the frozen initial scene and the frozen CRN seeds, produce finite and physically admissible observables. The CALIBRATION FEASIBLE DOMAIN of a parameter is derived by bisection from the frozen initial value towards the offending bound, with fixed settings (20 steps, relative tolerance 1e-3), always taking the feasible side. The derived domain is by construction a SUBSET of the registered range; the frozen parameter_ranges are not modified, and hand-narrowing or clamping remains forbidden. Measured trigger at the frozen settings: noise_relative_sigma at its upper bound 0.5 drives the distance mapping to -4.915 mm, which map_distance correctly refuses.
calibration_preregistration.bounds.physi.before: (did not exist) out_of_bounds_policy covered points OUTSIDE the registered range. Nothing covered a registered bound at which the simulator cannot produce a physically admissible result.

calibration_preregistration.evaluation_b.after: RECORDED AS AN OPEN FINDING, NOT SILENTLY FIXED. Measured on this machine at exactly the frozen settings: one four-class evaluation costs 60.8 s in an isolated probe, and 84 s averaged over the 140 scenario renders of the stage 0 run. The stated 2 s is therefore understated by about 30x, and the real single-threaded cost of the frozen budget is about 1,970 hours (82 days), not 65 hours. This amendment does NOT change spp, maxiter, popsize or restarts to make the number smaller: that would be choosing the experiment's resolution to fit the schedule. It is registered as a named blocker that must be resolved by an explicit decision before stage 1 begins.
calibration_preregistration.evaluation_b.before: "about 2 seconds per evaluation (64x64, spp=16, 128 bins, four classes, two passes each)", giving about 65 hours single-threaded for the 116,352 evaluations that AMD-003 derived.

calibration_preregistration.forbidden_pa.after: New confounded group CG-5_effective_medium. Measured within-stage cosine of the sigma_MC-normalised response vectors at the frozen settings: medium.bubble_density <-> _ALBEDO_BY_PRESET.bubbly 0.9995, medium.turbidity <-> _ALBEDO_BY_PRESET.water 0.9987, medium.mist_density <-> _ALBEDO_BY_PRESET.misty 0.9980; all three exceed the preregistered 0.98 threshold. Ruling, by the same rule used for CG-1 and CG-2 (fix the member with the weaker provenance, not the one that fits better): the three albedos are fixed as CONVENTION at their frozen initial values (water 0.60, bubbly 0.92, misty 0.88) and the three densities are fitted. Together with CG-6 this reduces the CANDIDATE search space from 20 to 15 dimensions; the ADMITTED set is not fixed here and must come from the CAL-PREREG-003 stage 0 rerun. CLAIM BOUNDARY: a fitted density may only be reported as an EFFECTIVE-MEDIUM extinction parameter of the calibrated simulator. It may not be reported as a true absolute concentration, turbidity or number density, because the value absorbs whatever the fixed albedo got wrong. This mirrors the CG-1 boundary, under which only sigma_t is claimable.
calibration_preregistration.forbidden_pa.before: (did not exist) The registry's CG-1..CG-4 do not cover the relationship between each class's extinction density and its single-scattering albedo. CAL-PREREG-002 stage 4 argued only that the three CLASSES do not cross-couple; it made no claim that density and albedo are separable WITHIN a class.

calibration_preregistration.forbidden_pa.after:
New confounded group CG-6_effective_angular_response, and it is a THREE-WAY degeneracy, not a pair. Projected over the six Empty observables that SCENE_GEOMETRY_SURFACE_FOIL declares:
  _BOTTLE_SURFACE_ALPHA <-> light.cutoff_angle_deg  1.0000
  _BOTTLE_SURFACE_ALPHA <-> sensor.fov_deg          0.9998
  light.cutoff_angle_deg <-> sensor.fov_deg         0.9998
Ruling: fix BOTH _BOTTLE_SURFACE_ALPHA = 0.02 AND light.cutoff_angle_deg = 25.0 as CONVENTION; sensor.fov_deg is the sole calibrated member. Provenance basis, not fit quality: the VL53L0X datasheet carries an external specification for system FoV, whereas the true VCSEL divergence and the bottle-surface GGX roughness have none. The weaker-provenance members are fixed. Note the simulator's sensor.fov_deg is a SQUARE perspective-film FULL angle and must not be treated as equivalent to the real system FoV, and light.cutoff_angle_deg is a HALF-angle simulator convention. CLAIM BOUNDARY: a fitted sensor.fov_deg may only be reported as an EFFECTIVE COLLECTION-ANGLE PARAMETER OF THE SQUARE-FILM RECEIVER SURROGATE. It may NOT be reported as the true or measured VL53L0X system FoV, because it absorbs whatever the two fixed members got wrong. It is also FORBIDDEN to simply set sensor.fov_deg = 25 and rewrite initial_simulation.lock on the strength of the datasheet.
calibration_preregistration.forbidden_pa.before: (did not exist) _BOTTLE_SURFACE_ALPHA and light.cutoff_angle_deg were measured at |cos| 0.9948 under the old global scope, and an earlier draft of this amendment ruled only on that PAIR, keeping light.cutoff_angle_deg fitted.

calibration_preregistration.stage_0.admi.after: max over the observables that p's OWN STAGE declares it optimises. Both numbers are recorded (max_leverage and max_leverage_declared). Reason: under the previous rule a parameter could be admitted on the strength of a channel its stage never minimises. Measured example at the frozen settings: _FOIL_SIZE_TO_DIAMETER_RATIO was ADMITTED at leverage 101.7 via Water-filled ambient, while its leverage on stage 3's own declared channels (Empty distance / signal / sigma_like) is 0.0006. Admitting it would have put a parameter into a stage whose objective terms cannot see it -- exactly the "fitted value decided by noise" failure stage 0 exists to prevent.
calibration_preregistration.stage_0.admi.before: max over EVERY observable: max_o leverage_sim(p, o) >= K admits p.

calibration_preregistration.stage_0.bord.after: A protocol-level, PARAMETER-AGNOSTIC conservative rule. If a parameter's own-stage leverage lands in the band and no NAMED secondary adjudication rule existed for it before this amendment, the outcome is GAUGE_FIXED_AT_FROZEN_INITIAL_VALUE. Inventing a rescue criterion for an individual borderline parameter is forbidden. The ONLY named exception is MAPPING_SIGMA.sigma_snr_weight, for which S0-B1..B5 was defined in advance and must be executed. BORDERLINE therefore ceases to be a blocker; only a parameter still awaiting its named secondary criterion, or one whose secondary criterion was not executed in full (SECONDARY_INCOMPLETE), remains unresolved.
calibration_preregistration.stage_0.bord.before: A parameter whose leverage fell inside the borderline band [5, 20] halted the flow with STAGE0_ADJUDICATION_REQUIRED and had no resolution rule, so every borderline parameter invited a bespoke ruling made after its number was already known.

calibration_preregistration.stage_0.coll.after: The collinearity blocker is computed ONLY over pairs that are (a) in the same stage, AND (b) still ADMITTED or ADMITTED_DETERMINISTIC after own-stage admission. The response vector uses ONLY that stage's declared observables, component-wise normalised by sigma_MC. A GAUGE_FIXED or NOT_ADMITTED member can NEVER form a formal confounding blocker. Reason: a degeneracy is a statement about the optimizer's search space. A parameter that is gauge-fixed is not in that space, so it cannot be confounded with anything -- reporting it as a blocker would demand a ruling about two quantities that are never fitted together. Restricting the vector to the stage's own channels follows for the same reason: the objective the stage minimises is the only thing that can fail to separate them.
calibration_preregistration.stage_0.coll.before: Pairwise cosine over ALL 20 optimizer dimensions within a stage, using response vectors spanning all 32 observables, with every pair whose |cos| >= 0.98 raising a formal confounding blocker regardless of whether either member was actually going to be fitted.

calibration_preregistration.stage_0.foil.after:
NO RULING IS TAKEN, and none is needed. Under own-stage admission, projected over the six Empty observables that SCENE_GEOMETRY_SURFACE_FOIL declares:
  _FOIL_REFLECTANCE_940NM       0.9065     -> GAUGE_FIXED
  _FOIL_SIZE_TO_DIAMETER_RATIO  0.0005576  -> GAUGE_FIXED
  _FOIL_SURFACE_ALPHA           0.5751     -> GAUGE_FIXED
  _FOIL_GAP_TO_BOTTLE_RATIO     10.64      -> BORDERLINE -> conservative
                                              gauge-fix by the generic rule
With no admitted member left, the admitted-only collinearity scope removes all three foil degeneracies as formal blockers. They remain CANDIDATE parameters in CAL-PREREG-003; whether they are admitted is decided by the rerun, not by this projection.
calibration_preregistration.stage_0.foil.before:
Three foil parameters were mutually collinear under the old global scope (_FOIL_REFLECTANCE_940NM <-> _FOIL_SURFACE_ALPHA 0.9986,
 _FOIL_SIZE_TO_DIAMETER_RATIO <-> _FOIL_SURFACE_ALPHA 0.9959,
 _FOIL_REFLECTANCE_940NM <-> _FOIL_SIZE_TO_DIAMETER_RATIO 0.9945),
which would have demanded a gauge ruling.

calibration_preregistration.stage_0.sigm.after:
Three deterministic branches with a preregistered relative floor SIGMA_MC_RELATIVE_FLOOR = 1e-12 applied to the observable's own scale:
  RATIO                  sigma_MC > floor            -> |delta o| / sigma_MC
  INERT                  sigma_MC <= floor and |delta o| <= floor -> exactly 0.0
  DETERMINISTIC_RESPONSE sigma_MC <= floor and |delta o| >  floor -> named
                         branch, outcome ADMITTED_DETERMINISTIC
No branch returns infinity and none invents a large number. INERT means the observable carries no information about the parameter, which is a leverage of exactly zero, not an unknown. DETERMINISTIC_RESPONSE means a noiseless observable that nevertheless moves, which is the strongest possible identifiability evidence and is recorded under its own name so it can be reviewed rather than hidden inside an infinity.
calibration_preregistration.stage_0.sigm.before: sigma_MC <= 0 made the leverage "undefined" and the parameter UNDETERMINED. One branch covered two opposite situations.

calibration_preregistration.stagewise.AM.after: The claim is corrected to its measured scope: Ambient is independent of the VCSEL EMISSION PARAMETERS, not of the scene. The AMBIENT_ONLY pass keeps the identical geometry, so the room light illuminates the same foil, bottle wall and participating media. Measured in stage 0 at the frozen settings, scene and media parameters move the ambient channel by 69-129 sigma_MC, which is LARGER than their effect on any other channel: _FOIL_SURFACE_ALPHA 112.3, _FOIL_SIZE_TO_DIAMETER_RATIO 101.7, _FOIL_REFLECTANCE_940NM 69.43, _FOIL_GAP_TO_BOTTLE_RATIO 108.7, medium.bubble_density 129.1, medium.turbidity 93.56, medium.mist_density 92.33. Fitting and freezing the ambient mapping first therefore pins a gain against an observable that stages 1-2 then move by up to two orders of magnitude of its own noise floor.
calibration_preregistration.stagewise.AM.before: "Ambient is obtained only from the AMBIENT_ONLY pass (VCSEL off, NOTE-034), therefore it is independent of ANY parameter of the active pass." Evidence cited: irradiance 1.0 -> 4.0 leaves ambient at 3.603355 -> 3.603355.

calibration_preregistration.stagewise.MA.after:
A SECONDARY CRITERION, preregistered here BEFORE it is run and simulation-only, decides borderline members of the sigma stage. It is recorded as a fixed conjunction so that a known borderline value cannot be waved through:
  S0-B1 channel dominance   the parameter's largest leverage must fall
                            on a sigma_like observable
  S0-B2 monotonicity        the observable response must be monotone
                            across five equally spaced points spanning
                            the registered range
  S0-B3 seed stability      the sign and order of magnitude of the
                            response must hold on the independent
                            verification seed set {2001, 2002, 2042, 2004}
  S0-B4 collinearity        |cos| with every other admitted sigma-stage
                            parameter must be below 0.98
  S0-B5 no unphysical side effect
                            no evaluation on the five-point grid may
                            produce a negative or non-finite observable
ADMIT only if S0-B1..S0-B5 all pass; otherwise GAUGE_FIX. The measured value 17.16 is explicitly NOT a reason to admit, and the criterion may not be edited after it has been run. NO SEPARATE CG RULING IS TAKEN FOR sigma_snr_weight: S0-B4 already decides it. Projected from the frozen CAL-PREREG-002 artifact over the eight sigma_like observables the sigma stage declares, |cos|(sigma_snr_weight, sigma_multipath_weight) = 0.9959 >= 0.98 while |cos|(sigma_snr_weight, sigma_width_to_mm) = 0.9503, so S0-B4 fails against an admitted member and the preregistered consequence is an AUTOMATIC GAUGE_FIX. The binding value is the one the CAL-PREREG-003 re-run produces, not this projection.
calibration_preregistration.stagewise.MA.before: (did not exist) sigma_snr_weight measured leverage 17.16, inside the preregistered borderline band [5, 20], and CAL-PREREG-002 offers no resolution other than halting.

calibration_preregistration.stagewise.SI.after: Audited in stage 0 as required. The Signal channel is affected by later scene parameters at least as strongly as Ambient, and the effect was previously invisible because it is expressed relative to an enormous Monte-Carlo noise floor. Measured RELATIVE shift of the signal median across the registered range: sensor.fov_deg 1349.7%, medium.bubble_density 1119.1%, _FOIL_GAP_TO_BOTTLE_RATIO 330.8%, light.cutoff_angle_deg 191.4%, medium.turbidity 171.5%, _FOIL_SURFACE_ALPHA 91.3%, _FOIL_REFLECTANCE_940NM 85.9%. The same sweeps score only 0.0006-16.6 in sigma_MC units because sigma_MC/|value| for signal_rate_mcps is 0.35-1.25 at the frozen spp = 16, versus 4.6e-4 for distance_mm and about 1.1e-2 for ambient_rate_mcps. Conclusion: the Signal mapping must also be fitted last, and the signal channel's noise floor is recorded as an open finding (see evaluation_budget.wall_clock).
calibration_preregistration.stagewise.SI.before: signal_energy_to_mcps is a post-hoc unit conversion applied after the estimator, so it is determined by the class-pooled signal location. Only the three foil amplitude parameters were named as an approximate residual confound.

calibration_preregistration.stagewise.or.after: 1 SCENE_GEOMETRY_SURFACE_FOIL -> 2 SCENE_PARTICIPATING_MEDIA -> 3 MAPPING_AMBIENT -> 4 MAPPING_SIGNAL -> 5 MAPPING_SIGMA. Governing principle: physical scene and media first, final measurement mappings last. A mapping gain may not be fitted and frozen while a later stage can still move the observable it was fitted against.
calibration_preregistration.stagewise.or.before: 1 AMBIENT (mapping) -> 2 SIGNAL_SCALE (mapping) -> 3 GEOMETRY_SURFACE_FOIL (scene) -> 4 PARTICIPATING_MEDIA (scene) -> 5 SENSOR_SURROGATE (mapping). Stage 1's why_first claimed the Ambient stage "has no parameter in common with the other four stages, so doing it first cannot be overturned later".

calibration_preregistration.stagewise.ze.after:
A stage with no admitted parameter is a NAMED, LEGAL terminal state:
  status = NO_FREE_PARAMETERS
  optimizer_run = false
  physical model retained = true
  values = frozen initial values
  reason = failed preregistered identifiability admission
It is neither an error nor a silent skip, and the rule applies to any zero-dimensional stage. Loosening the admission threshold so that a stage "has something to do" is forbidden.
calibration_preregistration.stagewise.ze.before: (did not exist) A stage left with no admitted parameter had no defined semantics, so it would have been either an error or a silent skip.

surrogate.ambient.map_ambient_rate.jitte.after: `if jitter < 0: raise`. Zero jitter is permitted and is exactly deterministic; it also consumes no random draw, so common random numbers remain aligned between jitter = 0 and jitter > 0. Reason: 0.0 is the LOWER BOUND of the frozen registered range [0.0, 0.5] in initial_simulation.lock, and parameter_ranges sits inside the errata forbidden zone. The assertion therefore made stage 0 incapable, in principle, of evaluating a bound that cannot be changed. The original concern is not discarded: a constant ambient rate is now excluded by the objective itself, since J compares whole distributions by W1 and the real Ambient has non-zero dispersion, so jitter -> 0 increases the ambient terms and the optimizer rejects it. A distribution distance is a more precise guard than an assertion that also blocks a legal bound.
surrogate.ambient.map_ambient_rate.jitte.before: `if jitter <= 0: raise CalibrationError(...)`, justified as SRC-SAI §10's ban on a constant per-class ambient rate.

invariants_preserved.amendment_append_only: AMD-001, AMD-002 and AMD-003 are untouched. CAL-PREREG-001 and CAL-PREREG-002 remain frozen and readable; CAL-PREREG-002 becomes superseded and not-to-be-executed, exactly as CAL-PREREG-001 did.
invariants_preserved.bounds_resolution_hash: The single-path resolver from AMD-003 is unchanged. Removing the three albedo dimensions changes which dimensions are resolved, so the hash will change; it is recomputed and frozen into CAL-PREREG-003.
invariants_preserved.estimator: Unchanged. LEADING_EDGE with detection_threshold_sigma 5.0 and min_return_bins 2, as selected by the independent estimator preregistration and frozen into initial_simulation.lock.
invariants_preserved.first_access_ordering: Unchanged and still enforced. Stage 0 must complete and freeze before the first calibration access; this amendment is itself taken before that access.
invariants_preserved.heldout_seal: Unchanged. held-out remains sealed with access_count 0 until E1 final.
invariants_preserved.initial_simulation_lock: Not modified. payload_hash dc15c9543a3aecacafcd1cbc110c48fc5fdd08d28457d4859d2a0bf573cb8335 still stands, including every entry of parameter_ranges. The feasible domain introduced here is a DERIVED SUBSET recorded alongside the frozen range, not a replacement for it.
invariants_preserved.objective_function: Unchanged. J is still the uniformly weighted sum of 16 class x feature normalised Wasserstein terms, with s_f the frozen pooled IQR of the calibration split, computed once at stage 1 start.
invariants_preserved.parameter_registry: Not modified. parameter_set_hash 3bd65b50264413e6249d1d19cc900a8487673f073a4e531b3c456b760a39ff69 is unchanged. CG-5 is recorded in the preregistration's gauge_fixed list, exactly where CG-1/CG-2/CG-3's fixed members are already recorded, rather than by editing a registry whose hash is frozen inside the lock.

projected_open_blockers_after_this_amend:
SCENE_GEOMETRY_SURFACE_FOIL retains a three-way degeneracy among ADMITTED members: _BOTTLE_SURFACE_ALPHA <-> light.cutoff_angle_deg 1.0000, _BOTTLE_SURFACE_ALPHA <-> sensor.fov_deg 0.9998, light.cutoff_angle_deg <-> sensor.fov_deg 0.9998. CG-6 fixes _BOTTLE_SURFACE_ALPHA, but light.cutoff_angle_deg <-> sensor.fov_deg 0.9998 SURVIVES between two admitted members and is therefore still a formal blocker under the scope rule. NOT ruled here.
SCENE_PARTICIPATING_MEDIA would have ZERO admitted members (medium.bubble_density 16.59 BORDERLINE, medium.turbidity 5.293 BORDERLINE, medium.mist_density 0.9401 GAUGE_FIXED), and the S0-B1..B5 secondary criterion is scoped to the sigma stage only, so those two borderlines have no resolution rule.
_FOIL_GAP_TO_BOTTLE_RATIO 10.64 BORDERLINE in the geometry stage, also outside the scope of S0-B1..B5.
precondition_evidence.projection_basis: The own-stage numbers quoted in this amendment are PROJECTIONS recomputed from the frozen CAL-PREREG-002 stage 0 artifact (outputs/calibration/stage_0/stage0_identifiability.json), which recorded the full 20 x 32 leverage matrix and sigma_MC. They are valid as a projection because CAL-PREREG-003 renames and reorders the stages but keeps the same parameter groups and the same declared channel sets. They are NOT the binding result: stage 0 must be re-run under CAL-PREREG-003 and its output is what gets frozen.
precondition_evidence.why_this_is_not_post_hoc: Every number quoted in this amendment comes from a SIMULATION-ONLY probe. The calibration partition has never been read (count 0, ledger empty) and held-out has never been opened (count 0), so there is no fit result and no real-data comparison that these rulings could have been shaped to flatter. Stage 0 itself is not frozen, which is why its outcome is adjudicable at all rather than settled.

payload.rationale:
## Why the stage order had to change before any real data was read
CAL-PREREG-002 ordered the stages so that the two cheapest, most obviously identifiable mappings came first. The justification was structural: stage 1 claimed Ambient is "independent of any parameter of the active pass", supported by a measurement in which the VCSEL power was changed by 4x and the ambient reading did not move at all.
That measurement is correct and it proves what it was designed to prove: Ambient does not depend on the VCSEL. It does not, however, prove the much broader claim that was written down, because the AMBIENT_ONLY pass is the SAME SCENE with a different light source. Room light still reaches the sensor by reflecting off the foil, the bottle wall and the participating medium. Every geometry and media parameter therefore moves Ambient.
Stage 0 measured exactly how much, in units of the simulator's own seed-to-seed noise: 69 to 129 sigma_MC. For most of those parameters the ambient channel is the LARGEST response they have. Under the old order, stage 1 would have fitted ambient_energy_to_mcps against that channel and frozen it, and stages 3 and 4 would then have moved the same channel by up to 129 noise units. The regression guard would eventually have flagged SIDE_EFFECT_REGRESSION, but only after stage 3 had spent 38,784 evaluations, and the recorded conclusion would have been "the scene stage broke the ambient fit" rather than "the ordering was wrong".
The audit that this amendment required for the Signal channel found the same disease with an additional complication. In relative terms the scene moves Signal far more violently than it moves Ambient -- up to 1350% across a registered range -- but in sigma_MC units it looks negligible, because the Signal observable's own Monte-Carlo noise floor at spp = 16 is 35% to 125% of its value. Both facts matter and both are recorded: the ordering fix is necessary, and the Signal channel is close to unusable at the frozen sampling density.
The new order follows one principle: physical scene and media first, final measurement mappings last. A mapping gain is fitted only once nothing downstream can still move the observable it was fitted against.
## Why the admission rule now uses the stage's own declared observables
The previous rule -- max over every observable -- is what let _FOIL_SIZE_TO_DIAMETER_RATIO pass at 101.7 on a channel (Water-filled ambient) that its stage never optimises, while scoring 0.0006 on the channels it does. Admission is a statement about whether the optimizer can see a parameter; the optimizer only sees the terms in that stage's objective. Both numbers are still recorded, so the previous rule's verdict remains auditable.
## Why CG-5 fixes the albedo and fits the density
The three pairs are near-exactly degenerate (0.9980 to 0.9995), so one member of each pair must be fixed. The choice is made on provenance, not on which one fits better, exactly as in CG-1 and CG-2.
The single-scattering albedo values in the registry (0.60 / 0.92 / 0.88) are RECONSTRUCTED modelling assumptions with no first-hand source: nothing in SRC-PLAN or SRC-HANDOFF records the albedo of the water, bubble or mist preparations that produced this dataset. The densities are at least tied to a physically meaningful quantity through CG-1's already-fixed reference scale _SIGMA_T_REFERENCE_PER_M, and SRC-SAI §9 explicitly lists them as <validation-frozen range>, i.e. as quantities validation is supposed to determine. Fixing the quantity with no provenance and fitting the quantity the specification expects to be determined is the same ruling CG-1 made.
The cost is stated as a claim boundary rather than left implicit: a fitted density absorbs the error in the fixed albedo, so it is an effective-medium extinction parameter of the calibrated simulator and nothing more. Reporting it as a real concentration would be the same overreach that the CG-1 boundary already forbids for absolute turbidity.
Reversing this ruling requires identifiability evidence -- a measurement showing an observable that separates density from albedo -- not a preference.
## Why sigma_MC = 0 now has three branches instead of one
The single "undefined" branch conflated two opposite situations. An observable with no noise and no response tells you nothing about the parameter; its leverage is exactly zero and calling that "unknown" would halt the flow for a case that is fully determined. An observable with no noise that nevertheless moves is a perfect signal-to-noise ratio; calling that "unknown" throws away the strongest evidence available. Neither may be written as infinity, which is why the second case is a named outcome rather than a number. The floor is relative to the observable's own scale so that one rule covers channels measured in mm and in MCPS.
## Why the wall-clock finding is recorded rather than fixed
AMD-003 corrected the evaluation COUNT and left the per-evaluation COST as a stated estimate of 2 seconds. Measurement puts it at 61-84 seconds, so the frozen budget is roughly 82 days rather than 65 hours. The tempting repair is to lower spp, maxiter or restarts until the number looks acceptable, but every one of those choices changes the experiment's resolution or its search thoroughness, and choosing them by reference to a schedule is not a scientific argument. It is therefore registered as a named blocker for stage 1 and left for an explicit decision.
calibration_preregistration.stage_0.foil_group:
  before: >
    Three foil parameters were mutually collinear under the old global scope
    (_FOIL_REFLECTANCE_940NM <-> _FOIL_SURFACE_ALPHA 0.9986,
     _FOIL_SIZE_TO_DIAMETER_RATIO <-> _FOIL_SURFACE_ALPHA 0.9959,
     _FOIL_REFLECTANCE_940NM <-> _FOIL_SIZE_TO_DIAMETER_RATIO 0.9945),
    which would have demanded a gauge ruling.
  after: >
    NO RULING IS TAKEN, because under own-stage admission there is nothing
    left to rule on. Projected from the frozen CAL-PREREG-002 artifact,
    restricted to the six Empty observables that
    SCENE_GEOMETRY_SURFACE_FOIL declares:
      _FOIL_REFLECTANCE_940NM       0.9065     -> GAUGE_FIXED
      _FOIL_SIZE_TO_DIAMETER_RATIO  0.0005576  -> GAUGE_FIXED
      _FOIL_SURFACE_ALPHA           0.5751     -> GAUGE_FIXED
      _FOIL_GAP_TO_BOTTLE_RATIO     10.64      -> BORDERLINE
    Zero foil members remain ADMITTED, so all three foil degeneracies cease
    to be formal blockers by the scope rule above. This is RECORDED, not
    adjudicated; no CG group is opened for them. The binding classification
    is whatever the CAL-PREREG-003 re-run produces.

payload.title: Reorder the calibration stages so that physical scene and media are fitted before any measurement mapping is frozen; scope admission and collinearity to each stage's own declared observables; rule CG-5 (density/albedo) and CG-6 (three-way angular/surface response); add a parameter-agnostic conservative borderline rule and zero-dimensional stage semantics; replace the sigma_MC-zero and infeasible-bound cases with deterministic preregistered branches; and replace the wall-clock estimate, measured to be understated 30-42x, with a cost-model formula that is not itself binding
